note: Attacker-controlled 'Regex' property from the config file is fetched as a heap-allocated flb_sds; its raw bytes (here ending with a truncated UTF-8 lead byte 0xE0) become the regex pattern.
The pattern end pointer is set to the NUL terminator; the allocation holds exactly len+1 bytes, so reading past 'end' is a heap-buffer-overflow.

code: ret = onig_new(reg, (const unsigned char *)start, (const unsigned char *)end, ONIG_OPTION_DEFAULT, ONIG_ENCODING_UTF8, ONIG_SYNTAX_RUBY, &einfo);
note: Pattern and its end pointer are handed to the onigmo regex compiler; parsing happens immediately in onig_compile -> onig_parse_make_tree.

PFETCH advances the scan pointer by the encoding length. For the truncated UTF-8 sequence 0xE0 at the end of the pattern, onigenc_mbclen_approximate() returns (e-p)+needmore, pushing p past pattern_end.
The token end pointer is stored back to the caller; for the malformed final character, *src now points past pattern_end while the token is reported as TK_STRING.

Root cause: onig_node_str_cat trusts the caller-supplied (s,end) range and copies addlen bytes without verifying that end stays within the allocated pattern buffer, so an over-advanced *src causes reads past the heap buffer.
While parsing the regex branch into a string node, the parser appends the token range [tok->backp, *src) where *src is beyond the pattern buffer end for the truncated UTF-8 character.
Sink: len bytes are copied from the pattern; since the requested range extends past the pattern's NUL terminator, xmemcpy reads past the end of the heap allocation (heap-buffer-overflow READ).
